conclusions: Both hosts complete single and eight serial 48 MP inputs at 3200/.9 within the enforced output and aggregate budgets; original hash is unchanged and owned image/canvas/URL references return to zero.

The second recording has no screenshot records. About 963 MB observed total includes about 757 MB already-open host baseline; observed increase is about 205 MB, not eight simultaneously decoded 48 MP buffers.

After final full GC the median remains about 825 MB, about 68 MB above this recording baseline. GC-owned capacity/native caches/host state are not isolated; this residual is retained as a limitation, not called fully released or a proven leak.

The one critical event is retained explicitly and occurs during background transition, not the resource case. It is consistent with proactive background cleanup and does not itself invalidate 48 MP/8-image processing evidence.
Engineering defaults are closed for the tested static-image path. They are not universal safety guarantees, and production lifecycle/recovery validation remains necessary.
